record_verbatim.evidence: RETAINED REVISION-1 HISTORY - this field records what was observed when the finding was raised and must not be read as the current state of the file. The claims it makes about the file's contents described the file before remediation. See revision 3 of revision_history, remediation_performed, updated_evidence and resolution for the current state. Direct read of the file on 2026-09-29, lines as numbered in the file at that time. Line 19, under '1.1 Purpose', stated verbatim: 'Provides evidence for compliance with ISO 26262, IEC 61508, and other applicable safety standards'. Line 23, under '1.2 Scope', stated verbatim: 'Safety Requirements (ASIL-D, ASIL-B)'. Line 7 attributed the document to baseline commit 308028fb and line 8 stated 'Document Version: 1.0' dated 2026-09-11. One further defect found in the second review pass was not in revision 1: a document-control block near the end of the file recorded a named reviewer, a named approver and an approved status, an approval that had never taken place. Three independent checks contradicted or failed to support the claim. First, conformity: every indexed record carries human_approval_status 'pending', production_authorized false and product_verification_credit false, and the acceptance suite's own gate 'no production_authorized/approved artifacts' passes precisely because nothing is approved. No certification, no tool qualification and no third-party assessment record exists in the corpus. Second, IEC 61508: a recursive search for the string '61508' across the whole of docs/artifacts returned no match in any record. The only two standards in governance/standards-lock.json are ISO_26262_2018 (edition 2018) and ASPICE_PAM_41 (edition 4.1), locked_by 'safety'. There is no IEC 61508 requirement, mapping, analysis or normative reference anywhere in the corpus, so the document claimed compliance evidence for a standard the corpus has never ingested or referenced. Third, ASIL: the corpus does carry ASIL field values, FB2-SAF-SGO-000001 with asil 'ASIL_D' and FB2-SAF-FSR-000004 with safety_allocation.asil 'ASIL_B', so the letters are not invented. But the asil field on FB2-SAF-SGO-000001 carries NO justification field, and the corpus's own validator raises an open finding for it - 'safety goal FB2-SAF-SGO-000001 ASIL ASIL_D lacks justification' - so the value is an unjustified field on a synthetic record, not a derivation. Revision 1 further recorded that the concept-phase records that would justify an ASIL D determination were absent. THAT PART OF REVISION 1 IS NOW OUTDATED: FB2-SAF-FSC-000001 and FB2-SAF-TSC-000001 exist as of 2026-09-29. Their existence is recorded in closure_note and does not change the remediation, because both concepts are synthetic and each states in its own limitations field that it establishes no ASIL capability for any real product. The ASIL field remains unjustified and is still flagged by the validator.
record_verbatim.impact: RETAINED REVISION-1 HISTORY, with one premise corrected - see the sentence on the safety concepts below. Three distinct harms, in increasing order of seriousness. First, an internal contradiction: the document claimed compliance evidence while the corpus it describes is uniformly unapproved and unauthorized, so a reader who trusts the document will draw the opposite conclusion from the one the guard fields support. Second, a claim against a standard the corpus never engaged: naming IEC 61508 implies the lifecycle work was performed against a standard that was never locked, never mapped and never analysed in this corpus, which would misdirect any subsequent assessment activity toward work that has not been done. Note carefully what is and is not being alleged. foxBMS's own pinned documentation does list IEC 61508 as a candidate standard and cites IEC 61508-3:2010, so the standard is a legitimate consideration for the product and its removal from the sentence is not the remedy. The remedy is that the corpus performed no IEC 61508 work, so it cannot supply compliance evidence for it; if IEC 61508 engagement is wanted, the standard must first be added to the lock and the referenced records produced. This is what the revision-3 correction did: it removed the two IEC 61508-3 clause rows and added an explicit not-engaged note, rather than deleting the standard from the project's consideration. Third, and most serious for a safety corpus, an ASIL capability statement. Presenting 'ASIL-D' as an established characteristic of the corpus's safety requirements, when the asil field has no justification and the corpus's own validator flags it, is a safety-capability claim of exactly the kind this corpus exists to avoid making. A fourth harm was found in the second review pass and was worse than the first three in one specific way: a fabricated human-approval sign-off block near the end of the file named a reviewer and an approver and recorded the status as approved. An assessor who skimmed to that block got the exact opposite of the true state, and the fabrication was more likely to be believed than the disclaimer at the top of the file, because a sign-off block is what readers are trained to look for. The file also sits at the repository root rather than under docs/artifacts, so it is the most prominent document in the tree and the one most likely to be read first by a person who has not seen the generated views that carry the guard fields and the non-conformity disclaimer. No artifact was relabelled and no acceptance check was altered to accommodate this finding. CORRECTION TO REVISION 1: revision 1 recorded that the concept-phase records were absent. FB2-SAF-FSC-000001 and FB2-SAF-TSC-000001 now exist, so that premise is no longer current; see closure_note. Their existence does not reduce the harm, because they are synthetic and disclaim any ASIL capability.

record_verbatim.residual_risk: Closed by construction rather than by human discipline. The file this finding was raised about is no longer an independent document: it is a pointer, and the document it points to is emitted by docs/artifacts/tools/corpus.py cmd_render from the canonical records, byte-identically on every run apart from the timestamp. The residual risk this record previously stated - that the validator does not read the file, the renderer does not regenerate it, and the guard-field discipline has no authority over it, so it can drift back toward the overclaim with nothing detecting it - no longer holds for these paths. The earlier residual risk was real and is retained as evidence in revision 3 of revision_history: the revision-2 pass fixed the three defects it looked for and left a fabricated approval sign-off, a false provenance claim and two IEC 61508 rows in place, and no gate fired. THREE RESIDUALS REMAIN, and none of them is this finding: (1) a generated document can only be as honest as the records it derives from, so the corpus's own gaps - the `gap` and `partially_mapped` dispositions in the coverage plan, the absence of any target-hardware execution, the unverified ASIL justification - are reported by the document as gaps rather than closed by it; (2) the pointer files are hand-written, but they contain no engineering content, no figure and no claim, so the only way they can mislead is by being deleted, which `git status` shows; (3) the corpus's own coverage dimensions that are presence checks or declared constants - scope_accounting, export_reproducibility, semantic_consistency_checks, human_approval, production_authorization, and standards_mapping as a count of plan entries - remain presence checks or constants. They are not fixed here because no gate keys off them; they are now labelled **presence**, **constant** or **counted** in the generated document's own coverage table, so no dimension can be read as stronger than it is.

Verified defects and corrected: (1) a fabricated human-approval sign-off block (Reviewer/Approver/Status: APPROVED naming fictional corpus roles) survived at the end of the file and contradicted the READ FIRST header in the same file and all 220 corpus records - removed and replaced with a document-control table stating the real position; (2) the false provenance claim 'This document is automatically generated ... Manual edits will be overwritten on next generation' survived, which is false and told the next editor the authorised edits would be erased - replaced with a section stating the file is hand-authored, not generated, not under tool control, and therefore drift-prone; (3) two IEC 61508-3 clause rows survived in section 9 despite the revision-2 remediation record and commit message claiming they were removed, while the same revision's new section-9 preamble asserted the clause ids were the corpus's own references - rows removed and the preamble corrected; (4) the artifact-type definition table still carried a bare unqualified 'ASIL' at the point of definition - qualified; (5) several unmeasured '100%' and 'complete chain' coverage claims with no stated method were replaced by measured figures with named methods; (6) the STALE note pointed at the stale hand-written coverage-report.md as 'authoritative, tool-computed' - repointed at the live tool; (7) the mutation count contradicted the tool (said 6/20 functional, corpus.py check reports PASS for all 20) - corrected; (8) review and finding counts understated the corpus - scoped to their records and corpus-wide figures added; (9) the stated id scheme was wrong and several ids did not resolve - corrected; (10) scenario ids used the short key form inconsistently with the stated scheme - normalised. Also corrected beyond the review's list: a non-existent hazard id, four non-existent SW-TSR ids, a non-existent design id, a non-existent variant id, three non-existent baselines, a swapped parameter mapping, a mispaired test-measure-to-requirement mapping, a fabricated execution outcome, two duplicated glossary rows, a misnumbered section heading, and a '100% line/branch achieved' column with no coverage measurement behind it. This revision also corrects three stale fields in this record itself: the disposition_note asserted a corpus convention the corpus contradicts, the resolution still opened 'NOT RESOLVED, AND NOT RESOLVABLE', and root_cause/impact/resolution all still asserted that no functional or technical safety concept record exists.

revision_history.author: quality_engineer
revision_history.description: Durable fix implemented; the drift risk this finding recorded is closed by construction rather than by human discipline. The document is now generated. cmd_render emits docs/artifacts/views/traceability/traceability-document.md from the canonical records - artifact index, link registries, guard fields, coverage-plan dispositions and the coverage dimensions recomputed by the same function `corpus.py coverage` prints - using the existing view preamble, so it carries the identical 'Derived, not authored' / 'Regenerable' / guard-field / 'Not a conformity claim' contract every other generated view carries. Every figure is computed at render time; none is transcribed from a report or from prose. Two render runs are byte-identical apart from the Generated: stamp. The duplication is resolved by making the generated file canonical and reducing BOTH hand-authored copies - the repository-root file and docs/artifacts/reports/TRACEABILITY_DOCUMENT.md - to short pointers with no engineering content, and regenerating the .docx beside the reports pointer from that pointer so no third copy can carry stale content. In the same pass the coverage dimension negative_scenario_validation was found to have been counting scenario FILES rather than executing them; it now runs the mutation and change-lifecycle scenarios through the same path acceptance gate [5/8] uses and reports passes, and traceability_integrity was found to have read its dangling count from whatever findings happened to be in memory rather than measuring it, so it now re-runs link validation for its own figure. No gate was weakened, no rule changed and no scenario altered.

record_verbatim.root_cause: RETAINED REVISION-1 HISTORY - the causal account still holds, with one premise corrected at the end. The document was authored at the repository root on 2026-09-11, during the period before the corpus had a generated view layer, and it was written as a summary of the corpus's ID scheme and link structure rather than as a governance-controlled document. It therefore never passed through the corpus's guard-field discipline: it carries no 'Derived, not authored' provenance header, no human_approval_status, no production_authorized field, and no statement of what the corpus does not claim, all of which the generated views carry. Three habits produced the specific overclaims. The first is conflating a standards MAPPING with a standards CONFORMITY claim: the corpus deliberately holds a mapping from artifacts to ISO 26262 clause references, and somewhere in drafting, 'maps to ISO 26262 Part 2' was written up as 'provides evidence for compliance with ISO 26262'. Structural mapping is not conformity, and the corpus states this explicitly in the standards-mapping view. The second is conflating a field VALUE with a DETERMINATION: FB2-SAF-SGO-000001 carries asil 'ASIL_D' with no justification field, and the document read that as evidence of an established ASIL D capability. The value is real and traceable to that record; what is missing is the derivation, and the corpus's own validator says so on every run. The third, found in the second review pass, is worse than the other two because it is not an overclaim at all: a document-control block was written with a named reviewer, a named approver and an approved status, and no such review or approval ever took place. The names were drawn from the corpus's own fictional role vocabulary (safety_engineer, safety_manager), so the fabrication looked internally consistent to anyone who had read a corpus record. The IEC 61508 reference has no traceable origin in any corpus record. It was most plausibly carried over from the pinned source's own safety documentation, which does list IEC 61508 as an example standard that might suit foxBMS users, and then converted from a candidate-standard mention into an asserted compliance claim during drafting. That conversion from 'a standard we might apply' to 'evidence for compliance' is the same category of error as the ISO 26262 claim, and it is the specific step that is unsupportable. Finally, the file's location is the proximate cause of all of this surviving. Because it was written outside docs/artifacts, it fell outside every control this corpus applies: the validator does not read it, the renderer does not regenerate it, and the guard-field and non-conformity rules that govern every generated surface have no reach over it. That last fact is also why the revision-2 fix was incomplete: nothing in the toolchain could detect that the pass had missed the sign-off block, the provenance claim and the IEC rows. CORRECTION TO REVISION 1: revision 1 attributed the missing derivation to the absence of concept-phase records. FB2-SAF-FSC-000001 and FB2-SAF-TSC-000001 now exist, so the concept phase is no longer empty; the derivation is still missing, and the asil field is still unjustified, so the causal account stands with that premise replaced.

shape_note: Deliberately not shaped like a corpus record: no top-level id, profile, artifact_type or source_refs, so that generating packets cannot change any coverage number. See the module docstring of make_review_packets.py.

_contract.digest_note: The digests below are already filled in. Copy them; do not type them. Run `make_review_packets.py --transcribe FB2-REV-FND-000022` to have them printed as a pasteable block.
_contract.grant_is: any value other than "pending" or absent
required_elements: 2. approved_by - a named individual, not a role and not a team

3. role - a role_id declared in role-and-review-policy.json#/roles - plus independence{owner_role, satisfied, evidence, policy_ref}; the approving role must differ from owner_role AND from the author of the last content revision
4. date - ISO-8601, checked by grammar and by parse

5. review_packet{path, sha256, record_sha256_at_signing}; path must resolve to a packet.json on disk under docs/artifacts/reviews/signed ONLY - the regenerated tree docs/artifacts/reviews/packets is NOT admissible, because it is rewritten on every regeneration and would destroy your evidence; sha256 must equal that file's bytes now; record_sha256_at_signing must equal this packet's integrity.record_sha256; target.record_id and target.profile must both name this record

6. approval_ledger_ref{ledger_id, entry_sha256} naming your entry in docs/artifacts/governance/approval-ledger.jsonl. It is approval METADATA, not content: it is excluded from the record's content digest and is never a revision_history entry, so recording it neither bumps the revision nor stales a link. NEVER record the approval in revision_history - doing so stales every link pinning this revision and invalidates every stored review digest. See docs/artifacts/governance/approval-ledger.md

signature_block._packet_sha256_note: The digest of this packet.json's own bytes. It is deliberately left null rather than filled, because a file cannot contain its own digest. Compute it with `shasum -a 256`, or use `--transcribe`, which resolves it.
signature_block._recording: Archive the signed packet under docs/artifacts/reviews/signed/<profile>/<id>.json, then record the approval as human_approval_status plus an approval_evidence.human_approval block on the record, plus approval_ledger_ref naming one appended line in docs/artifacts/governance/approval-ledger.jsonl. Do NOT add a revision_history entry: see docs/artifacts/governance/approval-ledger.md.
signature_block._rule: Empty by construction. No automated process may fill this. Filling it in is the only thing that changes human_approval_status on the record. As of 2026-10-04 (amendment APPROVAL-RULE-A1) the corpus rule human_approval_rejected is an EVIDENCE requirement, not a prohibition: a properly evidenced approval is ACCEPTED and keeps `corpus.py check` green, while a bare grant value is still rejected. What the validator reads is contract.approval_evidence_block below; it fails if any of its six elements is missing, and the finding names which.

signature_policy: The signature block below is empty by construction. This tool has no code path that writes a decision, an approval, a signature or an execution verdict. Filling it is a human action. As of 2026-10-04 (amendment APPROVAL-RULE-A1) the corpus ACCEPTS a properly evidenced approval rather than banning the value outright, so this rule now has to carry the evidence contract in full: see signature_block._contract. Since the same day (amendment APPROVAL-LEDGER-A1) the approval is recorded in the append-only ledger at docs/artifacts/governance/approval-ledger.jsonl and the record keeps only a reference to it, so recording your signature neither bumps the revision nor invalidates any review digest.
